trip.title: Pacific Coast Road Trip — Seattle to Los Angeles

travelers.notes: first time on the Pacific coast; all under 21 (US drinking age)

vehicle.notes: MODIFY RESERVATION: original was pickup 5 PM Aug 8 / drop Aug 13 ($663 for 6 days). New: pickup on landing Aug 8, drop LAX morning Aug 15 (8 days, est ~$1,060 — verify actual). Under-25 young-driver surcharge; put all 3 on contract to rotate drivers.

return.note: BOOKED. Morning flight — return the car ~7:30 AM and be airside by ~8:00 AM.

budget_usd.notes: Range $4,700 (frugal) – $5,500. Flights line still reflects old estimate — update with actual Aug 15 fare. Rental is an 8-day estimate pending the Hertz modification. Park fees include Mount Rainier $30/vehicle.

trip_log: ACTUAL Aug 9 (Day 2): did Rainier as planned, but ended the night at the Quality Inn in Kelso, WA (I-5 exit 39) instead of pushing to Seaside/Cannon Beach. Astoria dinner and the coast arrival didn't happen.

REPLAN Aug 10 (Day 3), COMPRESSED: start from Kelso ~7:15 AM, US-30 through Astoria. Day trimmed to the essentials — Astoria Column/Riverwalk (recovering the missed Day 2 stop), Haystack Rock from the sand, Cape Kiwanda lunch, Thor's Well, Heceta Head. Ecola SP cut (duplicate Haystack view, $10 + slow park road); Neahkahnie is a drive-by photo only; Hug Point/Sea Lion Caves/sandboarding stay cut. Bandon ~6:45 PM — relaxed Face Rock sunset.

TRADE Aug 10: sandboarding (Sand Master Park, Florence, 4:45-6:30 PM) is back IN; Bandon is OUT — sleep Coos Bay instead. Night-drive-to-Brookings idea rejected: ~3 hr of dark curvy 101 past everything scenic, breaking the no-night-driving rule, to save ~90 min. Instead: Coos Bay by ~7:40 PM (daylight), depart 7:15 AM, Samuel Boardman by 9:30 with 2 hours in morning light.
decisions_made: Extended trip to Aug 15 (8 days, 7 nights) — return flight BOOKED: DL2568 LAX 10:59 AM -> SAT 3:59 PM
Added a full Mount Rainier day (Day 2): sleep at the Ashford gate night 1, hike Paradise/Skyline from ~6 AM, drive to the Oregon coast in the evening
Outbound now lands SEA 2:50 PM (not 12:27) — pick up the car immediately and drive downtown; the car-less Link light rail plan is dead
Added a full LA day (Day 7) ending with Griffith at sunset, sleeping near LAX night 7 — no more racing the beach day to a flight
Skipped Olympic Peninsula entirely (too far north, added ~200mi)
Skipped Sunrise side of Rainier (2+ hr from Paradise; doesn't fit with the evening coast drive)
Sleep in Salinas not Monterey (Car Week Aug 7-16 = sold out/$500+)
Sleep Garberville not Eureka (avoids 45min backtrack to Avenue of the Giants)
Sleep Pismo on night 6 (further south = shorter next morning to Malibu)
Skip Hearst Castle tour in favor of free Piedras Blancas elephant seals
User chose: surf lesson + otter kayak + SoCal swimming (declined ATV dunes)
hard_constraints: Mount Rainier: enter the Nisqually gate BEFORE 7 AM on Aug 9 — early entry has historically been exempt from timed-entry windows, but VERIFY 2026 rules on nps.gov and grab a reservation if required. $30/vehicle (or use an America the Beautiful pass). Grove of the Patriarchs remains closed (2021 flood damage).
Monterey Car Week Aug 7-16: do NOT book Monterey/Carmel/Big Sur lodging
Big Sur Hwy 1 open but Rocky Creek Bridge has 24/7 one-way signal control through Aug 31 (<=15min delay) - check Caltrans QuickMap
Fern Canyon requires free day-use reservation for Aug 11 (May15-Sep15 rule) + $12 CASH
Return flight is a MORNING flight: car back at LAX ~7:30 AM, airside by ~8:00 AM Aug 15

safety.warning: Sneaker waves on OR/N-CA coast surge 150+ft up beach with no warning; 24+ West Coast deaths since 2012. Cold water causes loss of limb control in seconds. Rules: never turn back on ocean, stay off beach logs, keep well up the sand. Swimming only in SoCal (lifeguarded, ~69F).
safety.mountain: Rainier: start the Skyline Trail early (parking + afternoon heat), carry water + layers (Paradise is 5,400 ft, weather flips fast), stay on trail — snowfields linger into August. Cell service in the park is near zero; download offline maps.

must_book_ahead: DONE: Ashford night 1, Hertz modification, Rainier entry (Days 1-2 are behind you; night 2 ended up at the Quality Inn, Kelso WA)
Fern Canyon day-use reservation for Aug 11 — TOMORROW; confirm it's booked + have $12 cash
Rooms still needed: Coos Bay (TONIGHT Aug 10 — Bandon dropped), Garberville (Aug 11), Salinas (Aug 12, Car Week), Pismo (Aug 13), LAX area (Aug 14)

days.title: Aug 8 · Land SEA → Seattle → Rainier gate
Aug 9 · Mount Rainier → Kelso
days.drive: 6 AM gate · stopped in Kelso for the night · ~130 mi

days.title: Aug 11 · Boardman + Redwoods
days.drive: 7:15 AM Coos Bay → ~7:30 PM · ~5.5 hr · ~270 mi

stops.name: SEA — Seattle-Tacoma Airport
stops.desc: DL1045 lands 2:50 PM. Go straight to the Hertz counter — with the later landing there's no car-less downtown window anymore. Wheels by ~3:45, downtown by ~4:15.

stops.name: Pike Place Market
stops.desc: Produce stalls wind down after 5, but the market, chowder, Piroshky Piroshky, and the gum wall are still going. Park once (Pike Place garage) — everything downtown is walkable from here.

stops.name: Waterfront + Seattle Great Wheel
stops.desc: Straight downhill from Pike Place on the rebuilt waterfront promenade. 175-ft Ferris wheel out over Elliott Bay, enclosed gondolas, ~12 min, big Sound + skyline views.

stops.name: Space Needle + Chihuly Garden
stops.desc: 5 min drive from the market. Go up the Needle, or (better value) the Chihuly Garden & Glass next door. Only if you're ahead of schedule — Kerry Park at sunset matters more.

stops.name: Kerry Park
stops.desc: THE Seattle postcard: skyline, Elliott Bay, and — on a clear evening — Mount Rainier floating behind the city. You'll be standing on its summit road tomorrow. Free, 5 min from downtown. Sunset ~8:25 PM; leave by 8 to make Ashford at a sane hour.

stops.name: Sleep: Ashford (Rainier gate)
stops.desc: ~2 hr from downtown. Ashford/Elbe motels and cabins sit 6 mi from the Nisqually entrance — BOOK NOW, it's an August Saturday. Campsite alternative: Cougar Rock (inside the park). Grab breakfast food + hike snacks tonight; nothing opens before 7 AM.

stops.name: Nisqually Entrance
stops.desc: In before 7 AM: historically exempt from timed-entry windows (VERIFY 2026 rules on nps.gov), no line, and first light on the mountain. $30/vehicle, card OK. Full tank in Ashford — no gas in the park.

stops.name: Christine Falls
stops.desc: 69-ft falls framed by a stone bridge, steps from the pullout. Classic quick shot on the climb to Paradise.

stops.name: Narada Falls
stops.desc: 168-ft curtain waterfall; short steep path to the base viewpoint for rainbows in the mist.

stops.name: Paradise — Skyline Trail
stops.desc: The best day-hike in Washington: 5.5-mi loop, ~1,450 ft up, to Panorama Point staring straight at the glaciers. August = peak wildflowers + marmots everywhere. Layers + water; snowfields linger — stay on trail. Shorter option: Skyline to Myrtle Falls (1 mi, flat).

stops.name: Reflection Lakes
stops.desc: The mirror shot of Rainier, right off Stevens Canyon Rd, 10 min past Paradise. Calmest water midday-ish; then backtrack out the Nisqually gate. (Grove of the Patriarchs is still closed — don't detour for it.)

stops.name: Slept: Quality Inn, Kelso WA (actual)
stops.desc: Where night 2 actually ended: Quality Inn at Kelso (I-5 exit 39), instead of pushing on to Seaside/Cannon Beach. Smart call — no midnight coast driving. The coast is ~2 hr away via the Lewis & Clark Bridge and US-30 through Astoria; Day 3 replanned to start from here.

stops.name: Astoria — Column + Riverwalk
stops.desc: The Day 2 stop you missed, recovered: climb the 125-ft Astoria Column on Coxcomb Hill for the 360° view of the Columbia mouth, grab coffee/breakfast by the Riverwalk. You drive straight through town on US-30 anyway. Out by 9:15.

stops.name: Ecola State Park
stops.desc: Cut to save ~1 hr: the same Haystack Rock you'll see free from the sand at Cannon Beach, plus a $10 fee and a slow narrow park road. Only go if you're somehow ahead of schedule.

stops.name: Cannon Beach — Haystack Rock
stops.desc: 235-ft monolith, puffins, tide pools at low tide. ⚠ Sneaker waves — stay up the beach, off the logs.

stops.name: Hug Point
stops.time: + 15 min · only if tide + time allow
stops.desc: At low tide, walk around the point to a hidden waterfall on the sand, sea caves, and an old wagon road carved into the cliff.

stops.name: Neahkahnie Mountain Viewpoint
stops.desc: Roadside pullout in Oswald West SP with a near-180° view — one of the highest on the coast. Easy to miss the turnout.

stops.name: Cape Kiwanda
stops.desc: Climb the big sandstone dune; lunch at Pelican Brewing right on the sand.

stops.name: Cape Perpetua — Thor's Well
stops.desc: Highest driveable viewpoint on the OR coast. Thor's Well & Devil's Churn best ~1 hr before high tide (check the chart). Captain Cook Trail to tide pools — safe, great.

stops.name: Heceta Head Lighthouse
stops.desc: Most-photographed lighthouse in Oregon, on a cliff over a cove.

stops.name: Sea Lion Caves
stops.desc: Elevator down to the largest sea cave in the U.S. — ~200 wild sea lions inside. Right on 101 just south of Heceta Head.

stops.name: Sandboarding — Sand Master Park
stops.desc: Back in the plan: world's first sandboard park, in the Oregon Dunes at Florence — rent a board and ride 40+ ft dunes for ~1.5 hr. CALL FROM THE ROAD THIS MORNING to confirm closing time and boards. Bought by dropping Bandon: sleep is Coos Bay tonight, 1 hr up the road.

stops.name: Sleep: Coos Bay
stops.desc: Coos Bay, not Bandon — the Bandon detour was traded for sandboarding, and stopping here keeps the no-night-driving rule (arrive ~7:40, sunset 8:24). Cheap motels, dinner in town, and tomorrow starts 7:15 AM sharp: Samuel Boardman by 9:30 in morning light, with 2 full hours there. Book the room from the road today.

stops.name: Bandon / Face Rock
stops.desc: Cut: sleeping in Coos Bay and skipping the Bandon detour buys Samuel Boardman two full hours in morning light instead of one.

stops.name: Samuel Boardman Scenic Corridor
stops.desc: North of Brookings — the best cliff pullouts in Oregon. Natural Bridges & Secret Beach. Lunch in Brookings before crossing into CA.

stops.name: Klamath River Overlook
stops.desc: High bluff over the Klamath river-mouth — the least-crowded great overlook on the coast. Gray whales offshore.

stops.name: Prairie Creek Redwoods — Fern Canyon
stops.desc: World's tallest trees. Fern Canyon's 50-ft fern walls are the showstopper — needs a free day-use reservation (for Aug 11) + $12 cash. Rough access road. Watch for Roosevelt elk.

stops.name: Avenue of the Giants
stops.desc: 31-mile old-growth scenic alternate to 101. Walk among the giants at Founders Grove.

stops.name: Shrine Drive-Thru Tree
stops.desc: Roadside classic on the Avenue: drive your car THROUGH a living redwood. Cheesy, quick, great photo.

stops.name: Sleep: Garberville
stops.desc: Just south of Avenue of the Giants — cheap motels, no backtracking. Sleep properly, fuel up for the Bay run tomorrow.

stops.name: Golden Gate — Battery Spencer
stops.desc: Marin Headlands overlook for the classic bridge-and-city shot — in daylight, not at 11 PM, because nobody is night-driving this trip.

stops.name: Elkhorn Slough kayak — sea otters
stops.desc: MAIN EVENT: Moss Landing has the densest sea otter population in California. Flat, calm, protected water — no surf, no cold-shock risk, otters/seals/pelicans within feet of the kayak. Book for Aug 12; leave Garberville by 7:30 AM to make the launch window.

stops.name: Sleep: Salinas (NOT Monterey)
stops.desc: 20 min inland and cheap — Monterey is sold out for Car Week. Rest up; Big Sur is tomorrow.

stops.name: Point Lobos
stops.desc: Cypress Grove / Bird Island loops at the north gateway to Big Sur. Small lot fills fast — get there early. China Cove is stunning.

stops.name: Garrapata State Park — Soberanes Point
stops.desc: Unmarked turnouts (numbered gates 13–19), empty bluff trails. The Big Sur hardly anyone stops for.

stops.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
stops.desc: The most photographed bridge on the coast. Use marked turnouts. Expect the Rocky Creek one-way delay (≤15 min).

stops.name: Pfeiffer Beach
stops.desc: Purple-tinged sand & the keyhole arch. Narrow access road, $12 cash.

stops.name: Nepenthe
stops.desc: Cliffside patio 800 ft above the ocean. Café Kevah below is cheaper.

stops.name: McWay Falls
stops.desc: 80-ft waterfall onto a cove beach. Overlook trail closed through 2026 — view from the roadside.

stops.name: Sand Dollar Beach & Jade Cove
stops.desc: Big Sur's longest beach + the cove where you can find washed-up jade in the rocks at low tide.

stops.name: Ragged Point
stops.desc: Last big pullout at the south end of Big Sur — short trail to a sweeping cliff view, plus café/gas/restrooms.

stops.name: Piedras Blancas Elephant Seals
stops.desc: Hundreds of elephant seals on the beach, free boardwalk. Better value than a Hearst Castle tour.

stops.name: Morro Bay — Morro Rock
stops.desc: Giant volcanic plug rising from the bay. Fish & chips on the Embarcadero. (Backup otter-kayak spot if Elkhorn didn't work out.)

stops.name: Sleep: Pismo Beach
stops.desc: Beach town, cheap motels, and it shortens tomorrow's run to Malibu. Walk the pier at sunset (~7:55 PM).

stops.name: Surf lesson — Malibu (Surfrider)
stops.desc: Leave Pismo ~7 AM (~2.5 hr). Wetsuit included — water's ~69°F here, the warmest of the trip. Surfrider is a long, gentle, forgiving break: the classic first-timer wave. Book for Aug 14.

stops.name: El Matador State Beach
stops.desc: Sea-stack photos, steep stairs to the sand. Quick stop after surfing (it's just west of Surfrider — grab it on the way in if easier).

stops.name: Point Dume
stops.desc: Short climb to a headland with a sweeping Malibu view; sea lions below.

stops.name: Santa Monica — swim + beach
stops.desc: THE swim stop: ~69°F water, lifeguarded, gentle. Pier, Route 66 sign — actually get in the water here. No flight to catch today, so stay as long as it's fun.

stops.name: Venice Beach Boardwalk
stops.desc: Skate park, Muscle Beach, street performers, the canals two blocks in. A short hop south of Santa Monica while you're already sandy.

stops.name: Griffith Observatory — Hollywood Sign
stops.desc: It fits now — no flight tonight. Free observatory, the Hollywood Sign view, and the city lighting up at sunset (~7:45 PM). Dinner near Los Feliz or on the way to the hotel.

stops.name: Sleep: near LAX (El Segundo / Inglewood)
stops.desc: Last night. Airport-adjacent motel keeps the morning drive under 15 min. Gas up TONIGHT (return the car full) and pack — tomorrow starts early.

stops.name: LAX — Los Angeles Airport
stops.desc: Return the Hertz car ~7:30 AM, shuttle to the terminal, airside by ~8:00. DL2568 departs 10:59 AM, lands San Antonio 3:59 PM. Trip done — 8 days, ~1,550 miles, one whole coast.
